title: SeaSPRITE — Wireless Surface Vessel Control
problem: A legacy wired joystick limited mobility and classroom flexibility.
goal: Build an affordable, modular wireless controller capable of at least 50 meters of reliable operation.
solution: Led a three-person team integrating two ESP32 controllers, Wi-Fi command transmission, DC motor drive and servo steering. Supported electrical wiring, prototype troubleshooting, system verification and documentation.
result: Reliable land-based communication at approximately 60 ± 5 meters, exceeding the 50-meter target; intermittent performance near 90 meters. Over-water validation remained future work.

title: PLC & Industrial Automation
problem: Industrial equipment requires predictable and testable sequencing and safe control of electrical inputs and outputs.
goal: Program and verify PLC logic, analog signal monitoring, and motor speed control.
solution: Built and troubleshot Allen-Bradley Micro820 training exercises in Connected Components Workbench; implemented ladder logic, timers, digital/analog I/O and VFD fan speed control.
result: Tested control logic, voltage thresholds and potentiometer-driven speed references on training hardware.

title: CNC-Milled Bottle Opener
problem: Convert a functional part concept into repeatable machining instructions and a physical component.
goal: Design, program and manufacture a precision bottle opener.
solution: Prepared AutoCAD drawings, generated Mastercam toolpaths for facing, drilling, pocketing and contouring, and applied CNC G-code.
result: Produced a physical metal bottle opener and documented its CAD/CAM workflow.

title: CNC-Turned Bishop Chess Piece
problem: A rotationally symmetric chess piece requires dimensional planning and careful turning operations.
goal: Model and machine a bishop chess piece using a CNC lathe.
solution: Configured Aluminum 6061 stock, created geometry and machining origins, simulated turning paths in Mastercam and generated G-code.
result: Fabricated a physical aluminum bishop chess piece.

title: Construction Materials Testing
problem: Construction teams need verified material properties and documented compliance with specifications.
goal: Support field QA/QC across active construction sites.
solution: Performed soil density and compaction testing, fresh-concrete slump and air-content tests, and rebar/formwork inspections; documented observations and coordinated with site personnel.
result: Produced inspection and testing records supporting construction quality verification.

title: Electric Vehicle Fleet Conversion Study
problem: Replacing a gasoline fleet involves large upfront costs and uncertain operating savings.
goal: Evaluate the economic and environmental feasibility of replacing eight university vehicles with EVs.
solution: Built Excel NPV, after-tax cash-flow, break-even and sensitivity models, including 1,000-trial Monte Carlo analysis.
result: Model projected $493,116 positive NPV, 3.94-year payback and annual CO₂ reduction from 451 to 50 metric tons; scenario estimates, not realized savings.

title: Sooper Dooper Looper
problem: A marble needs sufficient energy to travel through a vertical loop.
goal: Design a functional 3D-printed track informed by kinematics.
solution: Modeled track geometry in SolidWorks, calculated minimum release height and velocity with a 1.3 safety factor, and prepared PLA prints using Cura.
result: Created a track prototype and motion-analysis workflow.

title: Secure Web Application
problem: Account-based applications need organized authentication and user-data workflows.
goal: Develop a database-backed web application with registration, login and password reset.
solution: Collaborated on an MVC application and MySQL relational database, integrating interactive account-management pages.
result: Delivered academic application functionality for account registration and authentication.

title: Automatic Night Light Circuit
problem: An LED should respond to ambient light using an analog sensing circuit.
goal: Design and analyze a photoresistor-controlled night light.
solution: Applied Wheatstone bridge, voltage divider and Thevenin analysis; modeled behavior in NI Multisim.
result: Developed and simulated a circuit targeting a 2 V, 20 mA LED.

title: AC Filter Design
problem: Electronic systems need selective frequency response and signal conditioning.
goal: Analyze low-pass and high-pass filters against specified cutoff targets.
solution: Developed circuit models and transfer-function analysis, examining 1.54 kHz and 72.34 kHz targets with ±5% tolerance.
result: Evaluated filter response and amplifier design options using circuit simulation.

title: Water Infrastructure Design — Peru
problem: Communities in Lobitos and Piedritas face challenges accessing reliable clean water.
solution: Used weighted multi-criteria assessment to evaluate treatment facilities, storage and pumping, and rainwater collection.
result: Recommended rainwater collection as the highest-scoring conceptual alternative (64).

title: Portable Liver Transport System
problem: Organ transportation requires careful preservation and system reliability.
goal: Investigate design constraints and risk-reduction concepts for donor-liver transport.
solution: Researched perfusion approaches, stakeholder requirements, power and pump failure modes, and redundant-system concepts.
result: Produced conceptual reliability recommendations; not a clinically validated device.
